rules.title: RSO no-fault eviction relocation assistance
rules.requirement: For an RSO-covered unit, a landlord using a listed no-fault reason for eviction must file the required declaration or notice with LAHD before serving the tenant and must pay relocation assistance. Relocation assistance is paid per unit, due within 15 days of the written eviction notice, and the landlord must pay the higher applicable amount if more than one amount applies.
rules.key_value: Effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027: eligible household $11,000 if tenancy under 3 years or $14,400 if 3+ years/low income; qualified household $23,150 if under 3 years or $27,400 if 3+ years/low income; Mom & Pop owner/family occupancy amounts $10,550 eligible or $21,250 qualified; due within 15 days.

coverage.small_owner_exception: Mom and Pop properties may pay reduced relocation assistance for good-faith owner or eligible-relative occupancy only if the building has four or fewer rental units, the landlord has not used the provision during the previous three years, the landlord owns no more than four residential units and a single-family home on a separate lot in Los Angeles, and the eligible relative does not own residential property in Los Angeles.
coverage.other_unresolvable: Applies to units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance; the bulletin does not state the full RSO coverage test.
coverage.summary: Covers rental units subject to the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance when the tenant is displaced for a listed no-fault eviction reason.

rules.exemptions: Landlords are exempt from relocation assistance when evicting a resident manager to replace the manager with another resident manager, except a manager-tenant receiving free or reduced rent with no other compensation may be entitled; when eviction is required because of hazardous conditions caused by a natural disaster not caused by the landlord's negligence. A landlord may offset accumulated rent against relocation assistance except for certain governmental order-to-vacate or unpermitted dwelling terminations.
rules.penalty: Failure to file the Landlord Declaration with LAHD makes the eviction a violation of the RSO; in a possession action, the tenant may raise failure to provide relocation assistance as an affirmative defense and may file a complaint with LAHD or seek private legal advice.
rules.interaction: For demolition for new construction, tenants receive at least the RSO amount, increased only if the Housing Crisis Act or Resident Protections Ordinance requires a higher amount.
rules.quoted_span:
All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a 
Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) before 
evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause 
Ordinance (JCO).

rules.title: JCO no-fault eviction relocation assistance
rules.requirement: For a JCO-covered unit, a landlord using a listed no-fault reason for eviction must file the required declaration with LAHD before serving the tenant and must pay relocation assistance. Relocation assistance is paid per unit, due within 15 days of the written eviction notice, and single-family dwellings owned by qualifying natural persons have a one-month-rent relocation amount.
rules.key_value: Effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027: eligible household $11,000 if tenancy under 3 years or $14,400 if 3+ years/low income; qualified household $23,150 if under 3 years or $27,400 if 3+ years/low income; qualifying single-family dwelling owned by natural person: one month's rent; due within 15 days.

coverage.small_owner_exception: For a single-family dwelling subject to the JCO where the owner is a natural person, including certain trusts or controlled legal entities, who owns no more than four dwelling units and a single-family home on a separate lot in Los Angeles, the relocation amount is one month's rent in effect when the termination notice was served.
coverage.other_unresolvable: Applies to units covered by the Just Cause Ordinance; the bulletin does not state the full JCO coverage test.
coverage.summary: Covers rental units subject to the Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance when the tenant is displaced for a listed no-fault eviction reason.

rules.exemptions: Landlords are exempt from relocation assistance when evicting a resident manager to replace the manager with another resident manager, except a manager-tenant receiving free or reduced rent with no other compensation may be entitled; when eviction is required because of hazardous conditions caused by a natural disaster not caused by the landlord's negligence. A landlord may offset accumulated rent against relocation assistance except for certain governmental order-to-vacate or unpermitted dwelling terminations.
rules.penalty: Failure to file the Landlord Declaration with LAHD makes the eviction a violation of the JCO; in a possession action, the tenant may raise failure to provide relocation assistance as an affirmative defense and may file a complaint with LAHD or seek private legal advice.
rules.interaction: For demolition for new construction, tenants receive at least the JCO amount, increased only if the Housing Crisis Act or Resident Protections Ordinance requires a higher amount.
rules.quoted_span:
Single Family Dwellings Owned by Natural Persons  When the residential real property  is
a single-family dwelling subject to the JCO and the owner is a natural person, including
natural  persons who hold properties in a trust or registered legal entity controlled by   that
natural person, who owns no more than four dwelling units and a single-family home on a

rules.title: Relocation for demolition or conversion regardless of RSO/JCO status
rules.requirement: A landlord who demolishes the property or converts it to specified non-rental or ownership uses must provide relocation assistance regardless of whether the property is subject to the RSO or JCO. If a tentative parcel or tract map for condominium conversion has been approved, the tenant may elect to relocate before receiving a termination notice and the landlord remains responsible for relocation assistance.
rules.key_value: Effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027 relocation chart: eligible household $11,000 or $14,400; qualified household $23,150 or $27,400; Mom & Pop owner/family occupancy amounts $10,550 or $21,250 where applicable.

coverage.other_unresolvable: Applies when the landlord demolishes the property or converts the use to condominiums, stock cooperatives, community apartment projects, hotels, or commercial uses; additional details of covered properties are not stated.
coverage.summary: Covers demolition or conversion to listed ownership, hotel, or commercial uses, even if the property is not subject to the RSO or JCO.

rules.penalty: The bulletin states generally that in an action by the landlord to recover possession, the tenant may raise failure to provide relocation assistance as an affirmative defense and may file a complaint with LAHD or seek private legal advice.
rules.interaction: This relocation obligation is listed alongside RSO and JCO no-fault reasons and applies regardless of whether the property is subject to the RSO or JCO.
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord demolishes the property or converts the use of the property to condominiums, 
stock cooperatives, community apartment projects, hotels, and commercial uses, regardless 
of whether the property is subject to the RSO OR JCO (LAMC 47.06 & 47.07).

rules.title: RPO relocation and occupant protections for demolition for new construction
rules.requirement: An owner demolishing a Protected Unit for new construction within five years after filing the notice or declaration with LAHD must comply with RPO relocation requirements and pay the highest applicable relocation amount. The RPO also provides occupant protections including relocation, a right to remain until up to six months before construction activities, right to return if demolition does not proceed, possible right of first refusal, and tenant notifications.
rules.key_value: Option 1 standardized payments effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027 for lower-income households: $115,480 extremely low income, $96,750 very low income, $87,450 low income; financial penalties start at $250,000 per displaced unit.

coverage.other_unresolvable: Protected Unit status can depend on recorded affordability covenants, rent or price control within the past five years, whether the unit was rented by lower or very low income households within the past five years, or Ellis Act withdrawal within the past 10 years.
coverage.summary: Applies only to Protected Units that will be demolished for the purpose of new construction.

rules.exemptions: The regular RSO or JCO relocation rules apply if the units to be demolished are not Protected Units or are not occupied by a lower income tenant.
rules.penalty: Failure to comply with the RPO may result in financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances.
rules.interaction: The owner must pay the highest applicable relocation amount under State and City laws; above-low-income households receive Chart A RSO or JCO amounts, while lower-income households may receive enhanced RPO amounts.
rules.quoted_span:
Owners who demolish a Protected Unit for the purpose of new construction within 5 years after the 
filing of the Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD are required to 
comply with relocation requirements under the RPO.

rules.citation: California Government Code Section 66300 et seq.; Government Code 66300.6(b)(4)(A)
rules.title: State relocation protection for lower-income households displaced by demolition for replacement construction
rules.requirement: Lower-income households displaced because their units will be demolished and replaced with new construction must receive relocation payments consistent with the relocation benefits paid by public entities under state relocation law. In Los Angeles, tenants being displaced for new construction must receive at least the RSO or JCO amount, increased if the HCA requires more.
rules.key_value: Lower income households at 80% AMI or lower; relocation benefits consistent with Chapter 16 commencing with Government Code Section 7260, Division 7, Title 1.

coverage.other_unresolvable: Coverage depends on lower-income household status and whether the owner will replace demolished units with new construction.
coverage.summary: Applies to lower-income households displaced for demolition of their units where the owner will replace the units with new construction.

rules.exemptions: The bulletin states that only lower income households being displaced for demolition and replacement with new construction receive the HCA-level relocation payment; tenants should receive a minimum of the RSO or JCO amounts, increased only if the HCA or RPO requires it.
rules.interaction: The document states that landlords must pay relocation assistance in compliance with the State HCA or City laws, whichever is higher.
rules.quoted_span:
The City’s Resident Protections Ordinance (RPO) and the
State’s Housing Crisis Act (HCA) require that ONLY lower income households being
displaced for the purpose of demolition of their units where the owner will replace the
units with new construction must receive relocation payment consistent  to the
relocation benefits required to be paid by public entities
